card: Describe a teacher or mentor who had a lasting influence on your way of thinking.
pts: who the person is
how you came to know them
what ideas or habits they passed on to you
and explain how they have shaped the way you think today
model:
The person who springs to mind is a lecturer in constitutional law who supervised my undergraduate dissertation. I came across him quite by chance: I had gone to his office simply to ask for a reading list, and he ended up questioning my topic for almost an hour.

What set him apart was his insistence on precision. He would circle a vague word in my draft and write, What exactly do you mean? At first I found it exasperating, but gradually I understood that unclear language usually conceals unclear thinking. He also taught me to argue against myself, that is, to look for the strongest objection to my own position before anyone else could.

These habits have profoundly shaped the way I work. Whenever I form an opinion about a policy, I now ask myself what evidence would prove me wrong. Likewise, I try to define my terms before debating them, which has saved me from many pointless arguments.

If I'm honest, he was not an easy person to impress, and I rarely received praise. Yet that very strictness made his occasional approval meaningful. Looking back, I'd say he gave me something more valuable than knowledge: a method of questioning, which I intend to carry into my doctoral research.
tipAr: في مستوى C1 اربط الأفكار بعلاقات سببية (gradually I understood) واستعمل تعبيرات مثل What set him apart was لإبراز الفكرة.

card: Describe a person who has made a positive difference in your community.
pts: who the person is
what they have done
how people in the community have reacted
and explain what impact their work has had
model:
I'd like to describe a retired pharmacist in my neighbourhood who set up a free homework club for children in a rented room above a bakery. I'm not sure he realises how much influence he has had, because he's remarkably modest.

It started roughly six years ago, when he noticed that several local children were falling behind at school because their parents couldn't afford private lessons. Rather than complaining, he simply asked retired teachers and university students, including me for a while, to volunteer a couple of evenings a week. Today the club welcomes around sixty children, and it has expanded to include basic computer skills.

As for the reaction, it has been overwhelmingly positive. Parents bring pastries and tea, local shops donate stationery and the municipality has finally offered a larger room. Not everyone was supportive at the outset, though; some neighbours worried about noise, but they came round once they saw the results.

In terms of impact, the most visible change is that many of those children now pass their exams and aspire to go to university. Less obvious, but equally important, is the sense of solidarity it has created. It demonstrates that a single determined person can make the entire neighbourhood feel more capable.
tipAr: لا تُكثر الأوصاف العامة؛ استخدم أرقاماً تقريبية وأمثلة (ستون طفلاً، غرفة فوق مخبز) لتجعل الصورة واضحة ومقنعة.

card: Describe a place that has changed significantly over the years.
pts: where the place is
what it was like in the past
how and why it has changed
and explain how you feel about these changes
model:
The place I have in mind is the neighbourhood around my grandparents' house, on the edge of my hometown. When I was a child, it was a quiet area of orchards and dirt roads, where you could hear roosters in the morning and cross the street without looking.

Over the last fifteen years, it has been transformed almost beyond recognition. Most of the orchards have been replaced by apartment blocks, the roads have been paved, and a small shopping centre now stands where we used to play football. The main driver of this change has been population growth: as the town expanded, land became too valuable for farming.

My feelings about it are decidedly mixed. On the one hand, I can't deny the benefits. There is a clinic within walking distance, buses run regularly, and young families have somewhere affordable to live. On the other hand, I miss the stillness and the strong sense of neighbourliness. People used to know each other by name; now many don't even greet their neighbours.

What troubles me most is that the changes were largely unplanned. Had the authorities consulted residents and protected a few green areas, the development might have been more balanced. Nevertheless, I accept that places evolve, and I try to appreciate what the area now offers.
phr: The main driver of this change has been...
On the one hand... On the other hand...
tipAr: الجملة الشرطية المعكوسة Had the authorities consulted... تضيف قيمة نحوية عالية؛ جرّب إدخال واحدة منها في إجابتك.

card: Describe a piece of technology that you think has changed society.
pts: what the technology is
how it works or what it does
how people use it in daily life
and explain what effects it has had, both good and bad
model:
The technology I'd like to discuss is the smartphone, which I would argue has altered society more profoundly than almost any other invention of my lifetime. Essentially, it's a small computer, a camera and a connection to the internet, all in one device that fits in a pocket.

People use it for far more than calls. They pay bills, follow the news, find directions, attend lessons and even file official requests to public offices. In rural areas of my country, many families first accessed the internet through a phone rather than a computer, which tells you a lot about its reach.

The benefits are considerable. Information that was once available only to a privileged few is now at everyone's fingertips, and citizens can document events instantly, which strengthens accountability. Small businesses can also reach customers without renting a shop.

That said, there are serious downsides. Many people struggle to concentrate for long periods, and misinformation spreads rapidly. Furthermore, constant notifications can erode genuine face-to-face conversation; you often see friends sitting together in silence, each staring at a screen.

On balance, I regard it as a powerful tool whose value depends largely on how deliberately we use it, and I try to switch mine off when I study.
tipAr: البطاقة تطلب الإيجابيات والسلبيات معاً؛ خصّص فقرة لكل منهما واختم بعبارة On balance لتُظهر رأيك.

card: Describe a time when you had to work under pressure to meet a deadline.
pts: what you had to do
why the deadline was tight
how you managed the pressure
and explain what you learnt about yourself
model:
I recall a week last winter when I had to submit a full research proposal for a scholarship application. The call closed on a Friday at noon, but because of a misunderstanding about the date, I only realised on Monday that the deadline was so close.

The proposal needed a clear research question, a literature review, a methodology and a timeline, and I had barely started. On top of that, I had two exams that same week, so time was extremely scarce.

To cope, I drew up a strict schedule. I divided each day into blocks: mornings for revising, afternoons for writing and evenings for editing. I also switched off my phone and asked a friend to read my drafts, because by Thursday I could no longer see my own mistakes. Admittedly, I slept very little, and there was a moment when I seriously considered withdrawing.

In the end, I submitted it with twenty minutes to spare. As for what I learnt, I discovered that I perform better under structure than under panic, and that asking for help is a strength rather than a weakness. At the same time, I promised myself never to rely on last-minute effort again, and I now set my own deadlines a week early.
phr: a strength rather than a weakness
tipAr: اذكر ما تعلمته عن نفسك بصيغة ملموسة (أعمل أفضل بنظام واضح)، ثم أضف قراراً عملياً اتخذته بعدها.

card: Describe an occasion when you had to make a choice between two options.
pts: what the two options were
what influenced your thinking
which option you chose
and explain whether you are satisfied with your choice
model:
The occasion that comes to mind was when I had to choose between two scholarships for a short summer programme. One was in a technology company's training centre, focusing on data analysis; the other was at a law school, where the course dealt with human rights and anti-corruption.

Both were attractive for different reasons. The first would have given me practical skills that employers value, and the second matched my academic interests more closely. What complicated things was that I couldn't accept both, because the dates overlapped.

I was influenced by three factors. Firstly, I asked myself which experience would be harder to obtain later. I could learn data analysis through online courses, but a specialised legal programme, with experts and a network of students, was a rare opportunity. Secondly, I spoke to a lecturer, who advised me to follow my real curiosity. Thirdly, I simply imagined myself a year later and asked which choice I'd regret not making.

In the end, I opted for the law school, and I'm largely satisfied. The programme gave me contacts and ideas that still feed my research. Admittedly, I still wonder what the other path would have offered, yet I've since taught myself the basics of data analysis anyway.
phr: The occasion that comes to mind was...
tipAr: استعمل صيغة would have + اسم الفاعل الثالث (would have given) للحديث عن الخيار الذي لم تأخذه، فهي علامة على إتقان أعلى.

card: Describe an experience that tested your patience.
pts: what the experience was
when and where it happened
how you reacted
and explain what the experience taught you
model:
I'd like to talk about an experience that tested my patience to the limit: waiting an entire day at a government office to renew an official document. It happened about two years ago, and I had assumed it would take no more than an hour.

I arrived at eight in the morning to find a queue already stretching out of the door. Inside, there was only one open counter, the computer system kept freezing, and nobody could tell us how long it would take. Every few minutes, an employee would reappear to say that we had to be patient, which, unsurprisingly, did little to calm people down.

As for my reaction, I started off quite irritated and checked the time constantly. Eventually, I realised that getting angry wasn't helping anyone, least of all me. So I took out a book and began talking to the man beside me, a retired driver who had been through this many times. His calm attitude was contagious.

I finally received my document at around four o'clock. What the experience taught me is that frustration is often a choice, and that the real issue lies in poorly designed procedures. In fact, it strengthened my conviction that public services should be simpler and more efficient.
phr: tested my patience to the limit
did little to calm people down
tipAr: يمكنك تحويل موقف بسيط (طابور في مكتب) إلى فكرة أعمق ترتبط باهتماماتك، وهذا يضيف عمقاً لإجابتك دون تكلف.

card: Describe a goal you set yourself that required long-term commitment.
pts: what the goal was
how you planned to achieve it
what obstacles you encountered
and explain what keeps you motivated
model:
The goal I've been pursuing for the past two years is to build an international research record, so that I can eventually be admitted to a doctoral programme abroad. It's a long-term undertaking, and it requires consistency more than brilliance.

My plan has three strands. First, I read and write for at least two hours every day, regardless of how tired I feel. Second, I'm working on a number of articles, aiming to submit them to academic journals. Third, I'm gradually improving my English to a level where I can present my ideas confidently at conferences.

Naturally, I've encountered obstacles. Money is a constant concern, and as an independent researcher without an institution behind me, I sometimes struggle to access journals or find reviewers. There have also been moments of doubt, particularly after receiving rejection emails, which can be quite discouraging.

What keeps me going is a combination of curiosity and purpose. I'm genuinely fascinated by the questions I'm exploring, and I believe my work could one day contribute to fairer institutions. Moreover, I remind myself that every rejection contains feedback I can use.

By keeping the goal in view and celebrating small progress, I've found that the journey itself has become rewarding.
tipAr: الأهداف طويلة المدى تحتاج الحاضر التام المستمر (I've been pursuing) فاستعمله لتُظهر استمرارية الجهد حتى اليوم.

card: Describe a social or environmental problem you would like to help solve.
pts: what the problem is
who it affects
what could be done about it
and explain why you personally care about it
model:
The problem I feel strongly about is the lack of transparency in the way public contracts are awarded. It is not a flashy issue, yet it silently affects the quality of schools, roads and hospitals in many countries, including mine.

It affects ordinary citizens first and foremost, particularly those who rely on public services because they cannot pay for private alternatives. When money is wasted or diverted, they are the ones who suffer from overcrowded classrooms and poorly equipped clinics. Honest businesses are affected too, since they lose out to those with connections.

As for solutions, I'd suggest a multi-pronged approach. Governments could publish all tenders and results online in an accessible format. Independent bodies should be given the authority and resources to audit them. Technology can also play a role: for instance, software could flag unusual patterns, such as the same company always winning, so that investigators know where to look. Ultimately, though, none of it works without informed citizens and protected whistle-blowers.

Personally, I care deeply about this because I've seen how a poorly built school can shape a child's prospects. It also connects directly to my studies, which gives me the sense that I'm preparing for work that truly matters.
tipAr: اختر مشكلة تعرفها جيداً من دراستك؛ المعرفة الحقيقية بالموضوع تتيح لك مفردات دقيقة وحججاً مقنعة.

card: Describe an idea you have that you believe could improve the way people learn.
pts: what the idea is
how it would work in practice
what resources it would need
and explain why you believe it would be effective
model:
The idea I'd like to describe is an offline learning assistant for students in areas with unreliable internet. It would be an app, installed once, containing structured lessons, exercises and speaking practice, along with feedback that does not depend on a connection.

In practice, a learner would follow a short daily plan, say, twenty minutes of vocabulary, a listening task and a few sentences to repeat aloud. The app would record how often each word has been reviewed and bring back the ones that the learner tends to forget, using a technique called spaced repetition. Because everything would run on the phone, it could be used on a bus, in a village or during a power cut.

As for resources, we would need a small team to prepare high-quality content, a developer and, ideally, teachers to check the material. Costs could be kept low, since there are no servers to maintain.

I believe it would be effective for two reasons. Firstly, regular short sessions are proven to help memory far more than occasional long ones. Secondly, it removes the barrier of cost and connectivity, which excludes so many talented learners.

Ultimately, I see it as a modest way of making education more equal, and I'm already experimenting with a prototype.
phr: a modest way of making... more equal
tipAr: عندما تشرح فكرة جديدة قدّم مثالاً ملموساً عن يوم المتعلّم (twenty minutes of vocabulary...) فهذا يجعلها واقعية ومقنعة.
